newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea eases rules on securities trading.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea eases rules on securities trading.

text.p: South Korea's Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday it had relaxed some securities rules in a bid to help boost corporate direct financing and allow more foreign investment in the local bond market.
It also paved the way for stock-index options trading to begin from July 7.

The commission statement said it had revised securities regulations to allow foreign investors to directly buy from June 2 non-guaranteed convertible bonds issued by large listed companies and those listed on the Korea Stock Exchange.
But combined foreign holdings would be limited to 30 percent of an issue and the individual foreign ownership ceiling would be six percent of an issue.
Under the new rules, foreign investors would be allowed to buy listed bonds with a maturity of three years or longer issues by small and medium-sized companies.
The foreign shareholding limit on these was set at 50 percent. But there were no rules on individual ceilings.
The commission agreed to end volume controls on corporate bond issues but it maintained a rule limiting individual company issues to 100 billion won per month.
The new rules abolished a minimum credit rating requirement of BBB for non-guaranteed bond issues but set the term of any rating's validity at six months.
The commission also approved rules on stock-index options trading drafted by the Korea Stock Exchange.
South Korea would adopt a European-style options market, where options would be exercised only on the last trading day, which is the second Thursday of each expiration month.
The market would have two types of options -- KOSPI 200 call option and KOSPI 200 put option. The size of a contract was set at 100,000 won. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
